problem: Existing EQA methods either explore the present environment from scratch (active EQA) or answer from a single recorded episode (episodic-memory EQA); none can combine many past episodes with active exploration, and long-term image memory overflows VLM context windows.
motivation: Robots deployed for days to months accumulate thousands of images per run, yet most questions need only a few frames. Questions about routines, changes and future states require deciding when to recall memory, when to explore, and when to stop. Searching the joint space of past and new observations without structure is costly.
key_idea: Organize long-term robot memory as a series of time-indexed hierarchical scene-graph world instances (a 'Robotic Mind Palace') and let an LLM/VLM agent plan over instances, areas and viewpoints to retrieve targeted past images or explore the present, with value-of-information early stopping of retrieval.
insight: Structured, retrieval-based memory beats stuffing frames into context or using captions only: Mind Palace reaches 65.0% answer correctness vs 52.9% for Multi-Frame VLMs using 100 images, while retrieving about 23. Its advantage grows with the number of past episodes (Multi-Frame VLMs degrade under fixed image budgets). Recalling past object locations improves present exploration on past-present questions, and early stopping cuts retrieved images from 22.86 to 15.73 with only a 3.2-point drop in correctness.
method: Mind Palace generation: split long-term history into episodes by macro-temporal interval (hour, day, week); each becomes a world instance G_i indexed by a text time label.

Hierarchical scene graph per instance: viewpoint nodes (pose, image, detected objects, GPT-4o caption) clustered into area nodes (centroid, object list) by VLM or floor-plan areas; present graph G_0 starts with area nodes only and is updated during exploration.
Reasoning over LA-EQA: a VLM checks whether working memory h suffices to answer; if not, an LLM names a target object or concept y (e.g. 'something to make coffee').

Planning over world instances: two-step LLM reasoning picks a strategy (PAST_ONLY, PRESENT_ONLY, PAST_THEN_PRESENT, MULTI_PAST_AND_PRESENT) and an ordered list of at most 5 past instances, with a heuristic preferring past over present.

Planning over areas and viewpoints: LLM gives per-area probabilities of finding y, and a 3-step forward-search MDP planner minimizes expected path cost (constant cost for past retrieval, path length for present); the LLM then picks up to 5 viewpoints, which are retrieved from memory or navigated to.
VoI early stopping: an LLM prediction set of present areas with P≥1-q; retrieval stops if the set has one area or further retrieval cannot change the next area to explore (VoI=0).
Working memory update: retrieved or observed images and reasoning are stored in h_k, and the loop repeats until the agent answers.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for LLM, VLM, captioning and judging; open-source tagging models for detection; classical planner (legged-robot nav policy on hardware)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB images with robot poses; past episodic trajectories stored as scene graphs (pose, images, captions, object lists)
setting.action_space: three high-level actions (retrieve, explore, answer); explore goes to viewpoints via a classical path planner (legged robot policy on hardware)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D houses), NVIDIA Isaac Sim (large warehouse), plus real-world office and construction site
setting.privileged: Pre-collected past trajectories/memories (by task definition); floor-plan maps used for area clustering in real-world sites; no GT test-time info otherwise

numbers.extra: 150 questions over 5 environments; max 100 retrieved images, max 25 exploration viewpoints

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own LA-EQA (not a canonical benchmark); no official split, so 'test' is used as a placeholder. Per-question-type and per-environment results appear only in figures.
results: Mind Palace gets 65.0% answer correctness and 0.45 exploration efficiency, beating the strongest baseline Multi-Frame VLMs (52.9%) and the best active baseline Active EQA w/ Frames (43.7%, 0.29). It retrieves 22.86 images vs 100. Early stopping keeps 61.8% while retrieving 15.73 images. On hardware, a legged robot in a 1,000 m² office with 10 past episodes answered all 7 questions and saved 3–10 room searches versus a no-memory robot.
limitations: Answers are limited by the coverage of past trajectories (e.g. a hardware question about a vacant desk failed because daily one-hour walks showed it empty), and the agent cannot tell when its information is insufficient.
GPT-4o's semantic and spatial understanding fails on detection, counting, functional properties and assigning objects to areas; multi-object, multi-episode questions are hardest.
The benchmark is manually built (150 questions, 5 environments), so it does not scale; LLM question generation was ineffective.
